newsitem.title: UK: TransCo to cut charges by one-off 21 percent.
newsitem.headline: TransCo to cut charges by one-off 21 percent.

text.p: Britain's gas industry regulator Ofgas on Wednesday said it accepted recommendations from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, which is seeking a one-off 21 percent cut in TransCo's charges to gas suppliers.

Ofgas said the MMC recommendations will result in a 29 pound ($47.5) saving on the average domestic gas gas bill in the coming year, which is a tougher result for TransCo than most industry watchers had expected.
Gas pipeline operator TransCo is part of BG Plc, which was formerly called British Gas.
The MMC recommendations compare with a one-off cut of 20 percent proposed by Ofgas last year. This would have resulted in a 28 pound saving on the average gas bill.
Ofgas said the MMC report recommended TransCo trimmmed its charges after the initial 21 percent cut by inflation minus two percent in the following four years.
This is equivalent to Ofgas' proposal of inflation minus 2.5 percent when revised gas volume forecasts are taken into account, the regulator said.

In a response to Ofgas' statement, BG spoke of a "tough settlement", with TransCo's revenues expected to be hit by five percent in 1997/98. The utility said it would also revise its dividend policy, but added it could meet the targets now set by the regulator. ($1 = 0.610 British Pounds)
